offlineNextBoundary.meaning: Instant counterfactual arithmetic from naturally occurring legacy states; not evidence that spawn-enabled B naturally reached stuck/cap.
offlineNextBoundary.minimalNext: Executed as boundary-run01; see lateEnabledBoundaryDiagnostic. Arithmetic and actual branch are recorded separately.

limits: Continuation of the same two initial scenes, not four independent new scenes. All cut pair calls retained for both attackers.
After first responsive-AI input divergence, hits/health/pose are regression observations, not same-input causal effect comparisons.
Instant pair closure and passivity tolerances address Float32 native arithmetic; these are not gameplay naturalness thresholds.
Support windows are observations around natural state/limb changes, not a fresh-memory intervention or proof of stale memory being a bug.
Body speed/height/spin peaks include part, detached flag and life/grip context. Stand/survival does not prove human motion.

The fixed 30-second harness continues after death while browser main pauses after its round-over sequence. Both-alive combat and post-death stress results are separate; this run does not reproduce browser timing/emotion/input.

Candidate longest continuous cut episodes were .1083/.1500 seconds; legacy episodes reached .35/.7333 seconds. The shorter candidate sequences are different combat trajectories and not proof of improved resistance.
In LS B, both arms were eventually lost; in Z B the opponent died at12.2667s. Survival, victory and wound totals are not efficacy metrics.
The Z B player off-hand axial peak90.7446rad/s occurred at25.6417s after opponent death. It is retained as post-death harness stress, not ordinary browser combat nor an established centerline cause.
Before either fighter died, candidate living-armed joint gaps peaked2.5155/2.5698mm (LS scene) and3.1788/2.4064mm (Z scene). These are measurements, not human-motion acceptance thresholds.
Natural spawn-enabled B stuck/cap and onehand exposure remain absent. The late-enable diagnostic covers actual helper behavior in a pre-existing natural legacy stuck state, not B spawn incidence.

Of the16 head calls,15 occurred with both fighters alive and1 on the fatal step. Of22 chest calls,4 occurred with both alive and18 after opponent death; the latter are immediate after-death physics, not a healthy dynamic-opponent sample.

Late-enable affected42 actual stuck pairs with34caps and no instant passivity/reversal failure. Later target limb/sword axial peaks increased and AI input diverged after2steps; this is not full-body naturalness acceptance.

nextDecision.pending: Retain the current two-weapon optional B; do not promote all weapons. Any next contact-controller change should isolate the observed post-stuck axial increase before adding onehand/default scope. Reuse stored natural injury/gait transitions for the recovery gate.

lateEnabledBoundaryDiagnostic.scope: Late enable at a real legacy stuck pair while both fighters are alive/standing/armed/gripping. Existing baseline reused; no fabricated wounds, new source physics or seed search. Does not establish natural spawn-enabled B stuck frequency.
lateEnabledBoundaryDiagnostic.boundaryExactness: Entire native/control/input frame prefix through1925 exact; paired physical body snapshot and request/points/budget/timer at chest pair1926 exact. Baseline has no whole-world native snapshot at this late pair; only candidate one is stored.
lateEnabledBoundaryDiagnostic.interpretation: First capped impulse is a same-state effect. Later reactive AI/control can diverge; subsequent pose/health is a bounded regression observation, not matched-input efficacy.
